missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative description. 'Могила' stays in the nominative as the subject. 'Старая' and 'заброшенная' are agreeing feminine adjectives. A clean descriptive sentence.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Могилу' is the accusative direct object of 'нашли'. 'Нашего деда' is the genitive showing whose grave. A natural sentence about visiting relatives' graves.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'На могиле' uses the prepositional form 'могиле' after 'на' to mark location. 'Цветы' is the nominative plural subject. A common cemetery scene.
Strategic focus: Dative after preposition. 'К могиле' uses the dative form 'могиле' after 'к' to express approach. 'Солдата' is the genitive showing whose grave. A natural motion phrase.
Strategic focus: Genitive after preposition. 'Могилы' is the genitive required by 'около'. 'Дерево' is the nominative subject of 'растёт'. A good pattern for describing surroundings.
Strategic focus: Instrumental case. 'Могилой' is the instrumental required by 'ухаживает за', meaning to look after. 'Вся семья' is the nominative subject. A useful caretaking expression.
Strategic focus: Genitive after preposition. 'Могилы' is the genitive required by 'возле'. 'Памятник' is the nominative subject, described by 'каменный'. A natural location pattern.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Могилу' is the accusative direct object of 'искали'. 'Эту' agrees in the feminine accusative, and 'долго' adds duration. A good searching pattern.

Strategic focus: Genitive plural with quantity. After 'много' the noun takes the genitive plural 'могил'. 'Старых' agrees in the genitive plural, and 'на кладбище' is the location. A useful quantity pattern.
